question: The Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution were added by which amendment to the Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act** in 1976.
 
• This amendment inserted a new part, **Part IVA**, which is titled "Fundamental Duties."
 
• The Fundamental Duties are listed in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Initially, there were ten Fundamental Duties; an eleventh duty was added by the **86th Amendment Act** in 2002.
 
• The Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by law.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act**

 
 
• Passed during the Emergency period, the 42nd Amendment is also known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to the extensive changes it made.
 
• It aimed to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the strength of the executive and legislature.
 
• Besides adding Fundamental Duties, it also laid down the Directive Principles of State Policy as fundamental to the governance of the country.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A**
 
 
• Article 51A outlines the Fundamental Duties of the citizens of India.
 
• These duties include respect for the Constitution, the national flag, the national anthem, and more.
 
• One of the duties added was to promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act**
 
 
• Enacted in 2002, this amendment made education a fundamental right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• It also added the 11th Fundamental Duty, which requires parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to their children.
 
 
 
• **Non-justiciable Nature**
 
 
• Fundamental Duties are not enforceable by law, meaning no legal action can be taken for their violation.
 
• They serve as moral obligations for citizens to promote a sense of discipline and commitment.
